intro:
A number stepped by a − and a + at the ends, or typed straight into the field between them.

Both doors stay open on purpose: past a handful of steps, tapping to a value is worse than typing it.

The ends repeat when held — after a short delay, then faster — so walking from 0 to 200 is a press rather than two hundred. Everything reconciles through a single value, clamped to `min`/`max` and snapped to `step`.

For a value picked along a range rather than counted, use [Slider](/docs/components/slider).
usage:
<NumberInput defaultValue={1} min={0} max={10} />

const [qty, setQty] = useState(1);
<NumberInput label="Quantity" value={qty} onValueChange={setQty} min={1} />

examples.title: Controlled
examples.description: Hold the value in state and read it back. Every commit — a tap, a hold, or a typed entry — arrives already clamped and snapped.
examples.code:
const [qty, setQty] = useState(1);

<NumberInput value={qty} onValueChange={setQty} min={1} max={99} />

examples.title: Bounds and step
examples.description: `min` and `max` bound the value and disable the button that would cross them; `step` is both the nudge and the granularity the value snaps to.

examples.title: Formatted display
examples.description: `formatValue` owns how the number reads — units, currency, grouping — while typing still reads a bare number back.
examples.code:
<NumberInput
  label="Budget"
  defaultValue={40}
  min={0}
  max={1000}
  step={10}
  formatValue={(v) => `$${v}`}
/>

examples.title: As a form field
examples.description: `label`, `description` and `errorMessage` make it a first-class field, with the label doubling as the accessibility label and an asterisk from `isRequired`.
examples.code:
<NumberInput
  label="Guests"
  description="Up to eight per reservation."
  isRequired
  defaultValue={2}
  min={1}
  max={8}
/>

examples.title: Display-only stepper
examples.description: `editable={false}` keeps the buttons but closes the keyboard, for a value that should only ever move one step at a time.

examples.title: Haptic steps
examples.description: `haptics` ticks the engine on each step — the value feels like it clicks. It needs the optional `expo-haptics`, and is silent without it.

variantCode.size:
<NumberInput size="sm" defaultValue={1} />
<NumberInput size="md" defaultValue={1} />
<NumberInput size="lg" defaultValue={1} />

notes:
Runs controlled (`value` + `onValueChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`). The value is always clamped to `[min, max]` and snapped to the nearest `step`; the display rounds to `step`'s precision, so `0.1 + 0.2` settles on `0.3` rather than drifting.

Typing is allowed to be briefly invalid — an empty field, a lone `-`, a trailing `.` — because clamping every keystroke fights the person mid-number. The field commits on blur or submit, and reverts to the last good value when what is left cannot be read as a number.

The buttons repeat when held, and read the live value from a ref so a hold never strides off a stale number. Each is a separately labelled accessibility button that disables at its bound, so a screen reader is told when a direction is exhausted.

Pass `haptics` to tick on each step; it needs the optional `expo-haptics` and is silent without it.
